text: Two groups of accounts. One of them is a coordinated ring. Which one?

Left. Same words, seconds apart. An open weather service. Two years old. Not accused. Right. Six accounts. Five under a month old. By chance? About one in two million. And the caption? This is just my chill page. The caption says chill. The verdict says shill. Picked left? You just accused the weather.

Shill or Chill reads the live Bluesky firehose and groups accounts that act together. It weighs four kinds of evidence. Here, two fired. One shared link. And brand new accounts, where three in a hundred is normal. A verdict also needs odds under one in a hundred, and no organic explanation. Gemini writes the explanation. Never the verdict.

So why not flag every copy? In fifteen fifteen, Dürer drew a rhinoceros he had never seen. Europe copied it for centuries. Wrong? Yes. Coordinated? No. Copying is not a conspiracy. Coordination leaves receipts.

Trace any picture yourself, on desktop or phone. NVIDIA Nemotron reads the old German line. Oxylabs searches the live web for copies. The earliest one found. Other versions. A receipt for each. Verdict: chill.

Then we tried to break it. Gemini wrote a hundred and eight fake campaigns, hidden in recorded real traffic. It found two holes. We closed both. Our blind spot: slow campaigns from aged accounts. Zero of thirty five.
We grade ourselves in public. Zero of two hundred eleven organic bursts flagged. Bluesky later took down six point five percent of accounts we flagged. Random accounts? Zero.
Scan it, and trace one yourself. Shill or chill? We check the receipts.
